module: First steps and a safe learning workspace
title: Find your way around 1C windows without losing your infobase
goal: Recognize your infobase and working window and choose the appropriate action.

prerequisites.text: Be able to open your own infobase from the startup list.

sections.title: The configuration shapes the interface
paragraphs: Sections, commands and forms differ between applications. A universal instruction such as “press the third button on the left” ages quickly. Identify the purpose: a request list shows records, a request form shows one object, a report processes selected data. An empty list can indicate no records, a filter or restricted access. Test these hypotheses separately.

A1 provides a Nexus model with three requests. It supports learning to read rows and totals on a phone without an installed platform. The model is explicitly labeled and is not a 1C window. An actual empty infobase contains none of these documents; do not search for menus its configuration has not defined.

Start with three clues: the selected startup-list entry, the launch mode and the open window title. A command can move on screen while its purpose stays the same. Record the application, command and expected change rather than merely “click on the left”. Such instructions remain reproducible when window size or interface language changes.

sections.title: One name at three different levels
paragraphs: These are different levels of one model. An empty infobase still needs its catalog definition; the example does not claim all three windows are already available.

code.source:
Designer: Catalogs → Customers
Enterprise: customer list
Enterprise: one customer card
code.output: Distinguish an object type, a set of records and one record.

tables.caption: Step-by-step reasoning
rows: Enter values for the selected item.

sections.title: Catalogs, documents and references
paragraphs: Catalogs commonly hold relatively stable domain objects such as customers and services. Documents commonly represent events or operations over time. This is a useful starting point, while exact behavior remains configuration-specific. “Alpha” is a customer presentation; the relation should preserve object identity, not merely a copied name string. Two customers can share a presentation.

REQ-001 and REQ-003 refer to one invented customer. Renaming that customer should not create a second identity. Repeatedly typing names instead of retaining references causes inconsistent spelling and grouping. A2 examines items and references in the official environment; here, learn to recognize the relationship in a data set.

Customers can refer to a catalog definition, its list of items or one open card. Designer selects the object type. In Enterprise mode, a list displays multiple records and a card displays one item. Before the catalog is defined, neither its customer list nor its cards should exist. Do not fill in an arbitrary window merely because it contains a text field.

sections.title: Filters change the visible set
paragraphs: Search helps locate a record; a filter specifies membership conditions. Conditions can combine, so record every active restriction before diagnosing a result. Status = New selects only REQ-001. Customer = Alpha selects REQ-001 and REQ-003. Durations total 105 minutes for all requests and 60 for Alpha. These are arithmetic control values, not measured service productivity.

A zero-valued row and no row are different observations. A report omitting closed requests does not prove deletion. Remove filters, locate the source document and inspect report settings first. Sorting changes presentation order; it does not by itself change the sum of selected values.

Navigation history can return to a previously opened form, but it is not a data backup. Closing a form tab does not necessarily delete its object; persistence depends on the write command that was performed. This introductory exercise enters no cards. We identify context and close our own windows without changes; writing and reopening records are checked separately later.

sections.title: Return to the correct mode
paragraphs: You do not need another infobase or different permissions. Correct the way the existing infobase is launched.

code.source: You expected an object tree but opened an empty application.
code.output: Close your own window and open the same infobase with Designer.

tables.caption: Step-by-step reasoning
rows: A window is not the infobase.

sections.title: Verify a user scenario
paragraphs: Start with known input data and a goal, such as finding Alpha’s requests and explaining their states. Verify identifiers as well as row count: two wrong records still produce a count of two. Then inspect an empty selection to distinguish no results from a loading error.

Model controls select statuses and show request details. This trains navigation without persisting 1C data. Candidate notes are separate per course; moving to P does not automatically award A1 completion. Identify the observation source in your protocol: Nexus model or official platform.

When an interface differs from an illustration, compare meaningful landmarks: mode, object name, selected command and result. Do not force an empty infobase to display identical panels. To request help, provide these landmarks and the lesson step. License numbers, other people’s records and full-desktop screenshots are unnecessary for explaining navigation.

sections.title: Check your explanation
paragraphs: I cannot find familiar application sections. Sections depend on the configuration. This lesson needs only the startup list and Designer tree.
I treat search or history as a backup. They locate a window or record. Persistence requires writing and reopening; backup is a separate procedure.
I identify a button only by its position. Add application, window and command names. Position can differ by size and language.

selfcheck.feedback: Alpha is related to the first and third model requests.
Presentation order does not change source values.

selfcheck.prompt: Write instructions for another beginner, from the startup list to the configuration tree and back. Check them by reopening the infobase.
selfcheck.feedback: Specify infobase, application, command, result and return path. Avoid vague directions such as “click there”.

practice.title: Identify your window and return to the lesson
practice.task: Write instructions for another beginner, from the startup list to the configuration tree and back. Check them by reopening the infobase.
practice.environment: Your own empty file infobase; no demonstration or business configurations are required.
practice.externalRoute: Standard startup list, Designer and Enterprise mode

steps.title: Find your startup entry
steps.action: Select your own training entry. Read or write down its name and verify the selection before launching.
steps.why: A similar shortcut does not prove that the right infobase is selected.
steps.expected: The initial context is identified clearly.
steps.troubleshooting: If your entry is absent, return to the first lesson and check infobase creation. Do not open a random business entry.
steps.before: Your own empty training infobase exists. The previous session is closed.

steps.title: Locate the object tree
steps.action: Start Designer and open the configuration if the tree is hidden. Expand and collapse Catalogs, then Documents. Add no objects.
steps.why: Tree navigation changes selection rather than customer data.
steps.expected: You can identify the root and two metadata categories.
steps.troubleshooting: Empty categories are expected. If the tree is hidden, open the configuration rather than create another infobase.
steps.before: The initial context is identified clearly.

steps.title: Compare the application window
steps.action: Close your Designer and open the same infobase in Enterprise mode. Compare title and commands. Record that application lists do not exist yet.
steps.why: Distinguish an object that has not been created from a navigation error.
steps.expected: Explain the mode difference without searching for a nonexistent customer card.
steps.troubleshooting: If both modes cannot run together, close the first session. Do not bypass training restrictions by deleting lock files.
steps.before: You can identify the root and two metadata categories.

steps.title: Return using your own instructions
steps.action: Close only your application window. Follow your short instructions to reopen Designer for the same infobase, then return to this Nexus lesson.
steps.why: Repetition tests the instructions rather than memory of button positions.
steps.expected: The same context is found again; the infobase was neither deleted nor replaced.
steps.troubleshooting: Clarify application, command and expected window if the instructions fail. Creating duplicate infobases is not a navigation fix.
steps.before: Explain the mode difference without searching for a nonexistent customer card.

criteria: The metadata category tree exists; application lists and cards are not defined yet. Definitions are distinguished from records.
Identify the mode and commands; a panel-layout difference is not described as a lost infobase.
Specify infobase, application, command, result and return path. Avoid vague directions such as “click there”.
Reproducible instructions naming your own training infobase.
A tree/list/card table showing what is currently available.
Reopening the correct mode without structural changes.
Open the wrong mode of your own infobase, identify it by its window and return using the correct launch command. Do not use someone else’s infobase for this counterexample.
